concepts.why: Biblical-theological / Baptist and Catholic readers: Titus 3:5 says 'renewal by the Holy Spirit', not that the Spirit gives life, and the same verse already sits under 'Born again' with its fuller note; it is a duplicate here that blurs the two concepts. The other seven passages hold the concept (create / renew / live / poured out). Notes quoted exactly.

concepts.name: The new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Lutheran / Reformed (does the text say this?): only Rev 21:2 says 'prepared as a bride'; Rev 3:12 and 21:10 do not (the bride appears in 21:9, not quoted). The name therefore says more than two of its three passages. All three do say 'coming down out of heaven from God' (3:12 'comes down out of heaven from My God'; 21:2; 21:10), so that phrase, which is also the drafter's own earlier C line, holds the whole set. 'Bride adorned for her husband' stays as Rev 21:2's note and is already on the front page.

Dispensational / Reformed / Catholic / secular readers: the name says 'to come', which only Heb 13:14 says (with 11:10 and 11:16, where the city is looked for and prepared). Heb 12:22 ('you have come to ... the heavenly Jerusalem') and Gal 4:26 ('the Jerusalem above is free') are in the present tense, and Gal 4:26 sits in Paul's allegory of the two covenants, where traditions divide over Israel and the church; set under 'to come' it reads as taking a side. Move both to a plain secondary line, 'The heavenly Jerusalem / the Jerusalem above' (Heb 12:22; Gal 4:26), which says only what they say. Concept 11 then rests on Heb 11:10, 11:16, 13:14, three passages of one letter that each speak of the same city sought or prepared.

secondary_or_links: Secondary 'The river -> the water of life': Ezek 47, Joel 3:18 and Zech 14:8 do not say 'water of life' (Zech 14:8 says 'living water'; Rev 22:1 alone says 'the water of life'). Relabel with each verse's own phrase, e.g. 'The river -> water flowing from the house of the LORD; living water; the water of life', so the line does not put Revelation's words in the prophets' mouths or imply Ezekiel points to Revelation.

Secondary 'All things -> renewed; restored; brought together; reconciled': acceptable as it states four phrases from four verses and names no persons, which keeps it clear of the universalism dispute (Reformed / Lutheran / Catholic would object only if it said 'all people'). But Matt 19:28's full verse brings in 'judging the twelve tribes of Israel'; if the line shows whole verses, show only the clause 'in the renewal of all things' there so the Israel / church question is not opened by a line about renewal.

Secondary 'The earth -> mourns and withers' and 'The heavens and the earth -> wear out like a garment': accepted; each says only what its verses say, and neither claims a link to the new heavens. Eight further secondary lines accepted as they stand.
Links: accepted as a set of ten; Judgment is rightly restored. No change.
